inspection_scope: Reviewed both caption modes for independent variants t01 and t02 using ordered native-frame sheets, native start/mid/end frames, all 13 consecutive frames in each declared contact window, and the supplied non-semantic pixel traces. Gold references were used behaviorally, not for pixel matching.

gates.evidence: In both variants Bot has a clear mobile-size silhouette, focused eyes, and an extended arm visibly directed toward the source sheet. t01 additionally shows the arm-sheet cluster rising while the focused posture remains legible.

t01 maintains the hand-to-sheet anchor throughout frames 24–36 while the layered sheet rises. In t02, frames 84–96 show no visible lift, contact consequence, compression, or bounded reaction at the declared frame-90 contact.

t01 develops from a lower sheet position to a raised inspection pose during its first second, followed by the declared deliberate inspection pause. t02 remains effectively unchanged from frames 60–119; the supplied trace likewise reports only near-zero changes throughout the shot, so its active lift beat never occurs.

Both variants retain the distinctive Motif Bot and a readable paper hero with offset layers, folded corner, printed lines, matte field, and grounding shadows. The designed irregularity survives at native size.

The minimal-isolated staging visibly prioritizes the extended hand and folded sheet, with ample separation and a small plant accent. Caption and no-caption modes preserve the focal hierarchy without requiring room dressing.
At 360×640 without captions, Bot, grip direction, paper layering, fold, and the low-versus-raised state in t01 remain readable. Essential objects are neither cropped nor dependent on caption text.

violations.observation: Across every consecutive frame in the declared contact window (frames 84–96), the sheet and Bot remain in the same low presentation pose; the event has no visible contact consequence or local response.
violations.smallest_correction: Animate the existing hand-sheet cluster through a short upward displacement centered on frame 90, keep the hand locked to the paper edge, and add a small bounded paper-layer settle after the rise.

violations.observation: The declared dominant action never develops: start, contact, and final evidence show the same pose, and the near-zero trace persists for essentially the full two-second variant.
violations.smallest_correction: Give t02 a visible lower-to-raised progression before or through frame 90, then reserve only the final roughly one second for the purposeful inspection hold.

sampling_limits: No MP4 playback or audio assessment was performed. The contact events are strongly assessable from consecutive native frames, and the supplied traces corroborate duration of change but are not treated as semantic motion evidence. Outside those windows, action timing is inferred from ordered sparse frames plus traces; subtle antenna, plant, or paper-layer motion between unsampled frames cannot be fully established.

gates.evidence: Focused eyes and an extended, rising arm-sheet silhouette clearly express Bot's participant role.
Frames 24–36 show continuous upward travel with the hand remaining attached to the paper edge; no intermediate detachment is visible.
The lower starting state visibly develops into a raised inspection state by about 1.0–1.2s, followed by a story-motivated hold rather than an unexplained dead caption hold.
Offset sheet layers, folded corner, print marks, shadows, and the canonical Bot provide clear material and silhouette identities.
The isolated diagonal relationship between Bot's arm and the elevated sheet makes the lift the focal idea; the declared minimal treatment is visible and appropriate.
Without captions, the sheet's elevation change, layered construction, hand relationship, and Bot posture remain legible at 360×640.
The focused face and extended arm read clearly, although the pose alone cannot supply the missing lift action.
The complete frames 84–96 contact window shows a maintained static grip but no lift, compression, consequence, or bounded paper response at frame 90.
Frames 60, 90, and 119 are visually unchanged, the consecutive event window is static, and the trace is near zero across the variant; the requested dominant action is absent.
The layered printed-paper material, folded corner, Bot silhouette, and subtle depth shadows remain identifiable.
The hero sheet and Bot-hand relationship retain clear hierarchy in the justified minimal-isolated field.
The objects and grip direction remain readable without captions, even though the required state change is missing.
